question.worked_solution:
The variable $z$ is being *multiplied* by $6.$ To isolate $z,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $6.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

$$
\begin{aligned}6z & >-5 \\ \frac{6z}{6} & >\frac{-5}{6} \\ \frac{6z}{6} & >-\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $6$ from the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6z}{6} & >-\frac{5}{6} \\ \frac{\cancel{6}z}{\cancel{6}} & >-\frac{5}{6} \\ z & >-\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z>-\frac{5}{6}.$
